subject: Prod latency spike: KV lock-contention at peak — Acme Analytics

From: Kelly Thompson <kelly.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: ops-eng@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 22 Aug 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sharp P99/5xx increase — need help

Connor —

We just hit a severe tail-latency event in production starting ~07:50 UTC. P99 jumped from ~400ms to ~3.2s and 5xxs climbed to ~2.1% over the last 30m. Throughput looks down ~30% on the inference lane for tenant acme-analytics-prod. Traces in the attached logs show repeated "kv cache lock wait" traces and many large-batch requests queued behind a single hot key.

Impact: API timeouts for our customer-facing feature (retries amplifying load), business-critical ingestion delayed. We're getting pages from SRE and customers are seeing errors. Can you confirm immediate mitigation options? Suggested immediate actions from our side: route traffic to a fallback smaller model, drop batching for the tenant if possible, or temporarily divert to a different lane.

I've attached a small logs bundle (logs.zip) with traces and a representative request/response. Let me know if you want a live call — ops-eng is on standby.

Attachments: logs.zip (stub)

Thanks,
Kelly Thompson
Head of Platform Ops — Acme Analytics

Date: 22 Aug 2027 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sharp P99/5xx increase — need help

Hi Kelly — thanks for the alert and the logs. I pulled the traces; I agree it looks like tenant-level hotkey activity causing KV cache lock contention and head-of-line blocking when large batched calls mutate overlapping KV ranges.

Immediate mitigation plan (can run now if you approve):
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens for tenant acme-analytics-prod to 4
- Disable prefix prefetch for that tenant for 60 minutes
- Move the tenant onto a high-priority dedicated lane (soft isolation) for the next 2 hours
- If needed, route a small percentage (10-20%) of traffic to the smaller fallback model to relieve load

I attached an incident-template with the runbook steps (short checklist). If you approve, ops-eng + I will execute a small canary (2 nodes) at 08:35 PT and monitor P99 / 5xx. We will keep you updated every 15 minutes and will rollback immediately if anything gets worse.

Can you confirm: (1) approve the config changes and canary window, (2) whether there is any scheduled batch job from your side that could be driving the hotkey pattern?

Attachment: incident-template.md (stub)

—Connor
Connor O'Brien

connor@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 22 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sharp P99/5xx increase — need help

Connor —

Quick technical read: logs show a tenant hot-key pattern where multiple large batches are attempting to access/evict the same KV partition set. That pattern is producing a "lockstorm" on the KV cache: one request holds a lock and many others queue behind it, causing HOL blocking and batch-lane starvation. Combined with our batch coalescing we get amplification because retries/replicated requests incur additional locking.

Proposed emergency changes (low risk to functionality, medium to deployment):
1) Reduce tenant max_batch_size -> 4 and max_batch_tokens -> 1024 for acme-analytics-prod
2) batch_delay_ms -> 8 (from 20) to avoid large coalesced batches under high concurrency
3) Disable prefix prefetch for tenant for 60m
4) Route tenant to a soft-dedicated lane with lane_weight 0.7 (reduce interference)
5) Canary on 2 nodes then extend to full pool if P99 & 5xx improve

Monitoring: we should track p99, p50, 5xx%, in-flight batches, KV lock wait time, and lane queue length. I'll push a mitigation-plan.pdf with the exact CLI/config snippets to Drive and tag the runbook.

Tradeoffs: average latency may tick up slightly, but tail and errors should drop significantly. If the tenant expects sustained high concurrency we should propose a short-term dedicated capacity commitment (2 weeks) — that avoids repeated incidents.

Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
